concepts.label: Articles (Definite & Indefinite)
concepts.summary: Italian definite articles (il, lo, la, i, gli, le) and indefinite articles (un, uno, una, un'), and how their form depends on the following noun's gender and starting sound.

concepts.label: Nouns: Gender and Number
concepts.summary: Italian nouns are masculine or feminine and pluralize by changing endings (-o/-i, -a/-e, -e/-i), with article agreement.

concepts.label: Numbers 0-100
concepts.summary: Cardinal numbers from zero to one hundred, including the elision rules for venti, trenta, etc. when combined with uno and otto.

concepts.label: Time Expressions
concepts.summary: Common time markers like oggi, domani, ieri, adesso, subito, dopo, prima, plus telling the hour using numbers.

concepts.label: Family Vocabulary
concepts.summary: Core family terms: madre, padre, fratello, sorella, figlio, figlia, nonno, nonna, zio, zia, cugino, cugina.

concepts.label: Food Vocabulary
concepts.summary: High-frequency food and drink words: pane, pasta, pizza, vino, acqua, formaggio, prosciutto, frutta, verdura, caffe.

concepts.label: Directions Vocabulary
concepts.summary: Spatial and movement words: a destra, a sinistra, dritto, vicino, lontano, qui, la, sopra, sotto.

concepts.label: Essere vs Avere
concepts.summary: The two foundational verbs essere (to be) and avere (to have): present-tense conjugations and the meanings each one carries (identity/state vs possession/age).

concepts.label: Weather and Seasons
concepts.summary: Weather phrases (fa caldo, fa freddo, piove, nevica) and the four seasons, all leaning on essere/avere idioms.

concepts.label: Present Tense — Regular Verbs
concepts.summary: Conjugating regular -are, -ere, and -ire verbs in the indicative present across all six persons.

concepts.label: Everyday Action Verbs
concepts.summary: High-frequency verbs of daily life — mangiare, bere, andare, lavorare, studiare, parlare, dormire — used in the present.

concepts.label: Present Tense — Irregular Verbs
concepts.summary: The most common irregular present-tense verbs: andare, fare, dire, dare, venire, uscire, sapere, potere, volere, dovere.

concepts.label: Ordering at a Restaurant
concepts.summary: Functional set for restaurants: vorrei, posso avere, mi porta, il conto per favore, plus combining food vocab with polite irregular verb forms.

concepts.label: Direct Object Pronouns
concepts.summary: Replacing direct objects with mi, ti, lo, la, ci, vi, li, le and where they sit relative to a conjugated verb.

concepts.label: Passato Prossimo
concepts.summary: The compound past tense formed with avere or essere as the auxiliary plus the past participle, including agreement when essere is used.

concepts.label: Imperfetto
concepts.summary: The imperfect tense for ongoing, habitual, or descriptive past actions, with regular -avo/-evo/-ivo endings.

concepts.label: Passato Prossimo vs Imperfetto
concepts.summary: Choosing between the two past tenses: completed events and changes (passato prossimo) versus background, habit, and duration (imperfetto).

concepts.label: Congiuntivo Presente
concepts.summary: The present subjunctive for opinions, doubts, wishes, and emotions after triggers like penso che, voglio che, e necessario che.
